source: a game where you adopt pets and trade them and there are 1 map and you can decorate your house and there are many stores and there are over 1000 pets that are Christmas, Halloween, easter and st Patrick days themed

image_prompt.text: Many enterable stores lining the town, plus the claimable player houses - pet shops and holiday-themed storefronts players go inside
A central, oversized gathering square where players meet to show off and trade pets
Walkable streets linking the square to the houses and the store strip, sized for foot traffic

layout_placement.text: Pet adoption points inside the stores where a player claims one of the pets

notes: The user asked for exactly one map, so no per-player interior instancing - P3 for enterable stores and houses, but no P4.
Over 1000 holiday-themed pets is content volume, not layout; nothing in the map changes with the count.
Trading is a player-to-player economy system with no stated physical location.

open_questions.ask: No look was stated - should the town read as cosy suburban, or take the holiday themes into the buildings too?
Do players decorate a house they claim from a pre-built set, or build one from scratch on their own plot?

coverage_missing.ask: What should the town itself look like - cosy suburb, or holiday-decorated year round?
Is the house claimed and decorated, or built from an empty plot?
How many stores is 'many' - a short strip or a full shopping district?

answers.ask: No look was stated - should the town read as cosy suburban, or take the holiday themes into the buildings too?
answers.answer: Make it a cosy suburban town, with the holiday themes focused on the pets and seasonal store decorations rather than changing every building.

answers.ask: Do players decorate a house they claim from a pre-built set, or build one from scratch on their own plot?
answers.answer: Players should claim a house from a pre-built set and decorate its interior; this keeps the housing simple and playable.
